questions.question: Who pays the input, and who sells it?
questions.note: End-market demand stability implies buyers (e.g., automotive/construction sectors) pay for input chemicals, while sellers (e.g., EMN) supply them.

questions.question: Is this capacity added or capacity destroyed?
questions.note: Capacity is neither added nor destroyed; demand rebound and destocking end stabilize supply-demand balance (no net change).

questions.question: Which listed substitute wins if the primary supply is missing?
questions.note: No clear substitute cited in the article for primary chemical supply.
